title: Microsoft Entra ID / Azure Sourcetype Reference
description: A multi-sourcetype registry, not a single event shape: these data sources primarily come from the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Azure (legacy -- now largely migrated/unsupported) and the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (MSCS), with some overlap with the Office 365 / Microsoft Security add-ons. Unlike the o365:metadata and o365:management:activity schemas, there is no shared Common Schema across these sourcetypes in the source dictionary, so each sourcetype is modeled as an independent branch under $defs, discriminated at the root by the always-present Splunk 'sourcetype' field. Several sections in the source dictionary describe fields conceptually/in prose rather than as exact camelCase API field names (notably Azure Metrics and Azure Topology) -- those branches are deliberately left permissive (additionalProperties: true, no invented property keys) rather than asserting field names not actually given.
x-primary-add-ons: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Azure (legacy -- largely migrated/unsupported)
Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (MSCS)

x-sourcetype-table.recommendedAddOn: Microsoft Azure TA (legacy) or Event Hub -> azure:monitor:aad via MSCS
x-sourcetype-table.notes: Interactive only in older TA; full sign-ins via Event Hub preferred

x-sourcetype-table.recommendedAddOn: Azure TA / O365 TA (Entra ID Metadata)

primarySourcetypes: (via o365:metadata or Graph -- no distinct legacy sourcetype)

x-sourcetype-table.recommendedAddOn: Archived add-on -> migrate to MSCS Event Hub, Microsoft Security TA, or O365 TA

x-sourcetype-table.requestedDataSource: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Alerts and Tasks
x-sourcetype-table.recommendedAddOn: Azure TA (legacy) -> MSCS or Microsoft Security TA

x-migration-notes: Preferred modern path for high-volume Entra ID sign-in + audit + risk data -> Azure Event Hub + Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (azure:monitor:aad).
Inventory (Users/Groups/Apps/Devices) -> O365 TA o365:metadata input is the recommended current approach.
Microsoft Graph Security API add-on is archived -- do not start new deployments with it.
Defender for Cloud / Security Center data is evolving toward Microsoft Defender XDR / Microsoft Security add-on.

signinEvent.description: Microsoft Entra ID Interactive Sign-ins (Graph sign-in logs). CIM: Authentication (strong).

status.description: Listed alongside errorCode/failureReason in the source dictionary; not given as a nested object there.

aadUserEvent.description: Microsoft Entra ID Users -- legacy Azure TA sourcetype. Inventory/snapshot event, the same conceptual object as o365_metadata_schema.json#/$defs/userEvent under the recommended o365:metadata sourcetype. Common useful fields per the source dictionary (not exhaustive).

aadGroupEvent.description: Microsoft Entra ID Groups -- legacy Azure TA sourcetype. Inventory/snapshot event, the same conceptual object as o365_metadata_schema.json#/$defs/groupEvent under the recommended o365:metadata sourcetype.

aadDeviceEvent.description: Microsoft Entra ID Devices -- legacy Azure TA sourcetype. Inventory/snapshot event, the same conceptual object as o365_metadata_schema.json#/$defs/deviceEvent under the recommended o365:metadata sourcetype.

aadAuditEvent.description: Microsoft Entra ID Audit (directory changes). Sourcetype azure:aad:audit, or azure:monitor:aad via Event Hub (the recommended modern path). Typical activities: Add/Update/Delete user, Add member to role/group, Consent to application, Reset password, PIM role activation, etc. CIM: Change / Account_Management, Authentication.

initiatedBy.description: user or app: userPrincipalName, appId, displayName. Nested under 'user'/'app' sub-objects here as a reasonable, commonly-known Graph shape -- the source dictionary lists the field names but not this exact nesting.

targetResources.description: id, displayName, type, userPrincipalName, modifiedProperties with old/new values.

riskDetectionEvent.description: Microsoft Entra ID Identity Protection -- risk detections & risky users. Sourcetype azure:aad:risk:detection (risky-user variants also exist). CIM: Alerts, Authentication.

riskEventType.description: e.g. unlikelyTravel, anonymizedIPAddress, maliciousIPAddress, leakedCredentials, etc. -- not an exhaustive enum.

riskState.description: e.g. atRisk, confirmedCompromised, remediated, dismissed, etc. -- not an exhaustive enum.

graphSecurityAlertEvent.description: Microsoft Graph Security API -- unified security alerts. Sourcetype GraphSecurityAlert. The add-on providing this sourcetype is archived; do not use for new deployments -- migrate to Event Hub + MSCS (azure:monitor:aad or security alert sourcetypes), the Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Security, or the O365 TA (for some CAS/Defender data). CIM: Alerts.

metricsEvent.description: Azure Metrics -- performance metrics. The source dictionary describes this content conceptually (Metric name, namespace, resource ID, Timestamp, time grain / aggregation, Value(s), Dimensions (resource-specific), Subscription / resource group / location) rather than as exact field names, so this schema intentionally does not assert specific property keys beyond 'sourcetype' -- see the description for the conceptual content instead. Usually stored in a metrics index when configured that way. Time grain / aggregation is one of: Average, Total, Maximum, Minimum, Count.

defenderAlertEvent.description: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Alerts (formerly Security Center). Sourcetype azure:securityCenter:alert. CIM: Alerts.

defenderTaskEvent.description: Microsoft Defender for Cloud Tasks (formerly Security Center) -- security recommendations / tasks. Sourcetype azure:securityCenter:task. The source dictionary describes this content conceptually (state, severity, resource details, remediation) rather than as exact field names beyond the two named here, so additional fields are not asserted -- see the description for the conceptual content instead.

resourceGraphEvent.description: Resource Graph -- results of Azure Resource Graph queries (Kusto-like). Sourcetype azure:resourcegraph. Fields depend on the project / query used; these are the commonly-seen ones.

topologyEvent.description: Azure Topology (both Auto and Manual collection -- same sourcetype for both). IaaS relationship / dependency graph, sourcetype azure:topology. The source dictionary describes this content conceptually only (resource IDs/names/types; associations/relationships, e.g. VM -> NIC -> NSG -> Public IP -> VNet/Subnet; topology nodes and edges; subscription/resource group context) without giving exact JSON field/property names, so this schema intentionally does not invent property keys beyond 'sourcetype' -- useful for asset inventory, blast-radius analysis, and visualization.
